desc: Producer-level canonicalization of logically-unordered maps. NOT a codec test: the byte-level canonical suite cannot decide these, because the same bytes are canonical as an ordered sequence and non-canonical as a map (see DESIGN.md 'Order Is Significant'). These vectors are consumed by layers that HAVE a map type -- the JSON object <-> C0 mapping, a schema-driven encoder, applications such as transfs. A producer given the `map` entries in the order shown MUST emit exactly `canonical`.

encoding.group: the group label (a name/identifier), or null for an unlabeled GS group
encoding.map: array of [key, value] entries in INPUT (pre-sort) order; the producer sorts them
encoding.key: a JSON string (logical UTF-8 bytes) or {"hex": ".."} for non-UTF-8/binary keys
encoding.value: a JSON string, {"hex": ".."}, or {"map": [[k, v], ...]} for a nested map
encoding.canonical: expected compact bytes as lowercase hex: GS label, then entries sorted by ascending byte-lex of each key's LOGICAL (unescaped) bytes, value bytes DLE-escaped minimally

cases.name: basic-sort
cases.desc: Two entries given out of order; sorted by key: host (0x68) before port (0x70)

cases.name: byte-lex-not-alpha
cases.desc: Order is by raw byte, not case-insensitive or locale: 'A' (0x41) < 'Z' (0x5a) < 'a' (0x61)

cases.name: logical-key-escaped-control
cases.desc: Keys are values and may carry escaped control bytes. Sort on the LOGICAL key: key 'a<HT>b' (61 09 62) sorts before 'az' (61 7a) because HT (0x09) < 'z' (0x7a) at the second byte -- even though the HT is DLE-escaped (10 09) on the wire

cases.name: empty-key-first
cases.desc: The empty key sorts before any non-empty key (it is a proper prefix of all others)

cases.name: nested-map-recurse
cases.desc: A value that is itself a map is canonicalized recursively inside STX/ETX (where the separator hierarchy resets): top level sorts 'nested' (0x6e) before 'z' (0x7a); the inner map sorts 'a' before 'b'
